newsitem.title: INDIA: India says trying to emulate Japan's success.
newsitem.headline: India says trying to emulate Japan's success.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, saluting Japan's economic progress, on Friday pledged to push ahead with free market-oriented reforms seen as crucial for transforming India into an economic superpower.

"In about 50 years, they (Japan) have raised themselves from a nation that was ravaged by war to one of the super economic powers of the world," Chidambaram told businessmen at the 12th Indian Engineering Trade Fair co-hosted by Japan in New Delhi.

"It is only a country that keeps it economy open, competitive, only a country that is willing to keep its deficit low, only a country that promotes thrift, only a country that values efficiency that can become a giant," he said.
"I believe we in India can also become a giant in our own lifetimes, provided we...persevere along the road we have taken in the past five years."
India, which in mid-1991 began a radical economic reforms programme, had risen to the second-most popular investment destination for Japanese firms in 1996 from the 11th in 1993, the minister said.
Chidambaram said India's capital goods industry had been strengthened, rather than strangled, by import liberalisation and was currently growing at a rate of 16.5 percent annually.
"The same will happen when we open the unopened sectors of India's economy. As we open up, these apprehensions that we have will be wiped out, will vanish," he said.
Japan is India's biggest aid donor but ranks only fourth in the list of foreign investors after Britain, the United States and Germany.

About 135 Japanese firms were present at the trade fair, which Chidambaram said was one of the largest engineering trade fairs in the world. The 13th Indian Engineering Trade Fair is scheduled to be held in 1999 in partnership with South Korea.
"In a way, I'm glad that Asian countries are helping us discover ourselves," he said. "Japan makes every Asian proud."
